packet.headline_seed: The world's carmakers are struggling to compete with China
packet.description_seed: The BBC visited China’s EV factories and found they are dominating the ecosystems shaping the global auto industry.

what: The world's carmakers are struggling to compete with China

clean_source_blocks.text: The BBC visited China’s EV factories and found they are dominating the ecosystems shaping the global auto industry.

Global carmakers are facing a reckoning as US, European and Japanese brands lose ground to Chinese rivals setting the pace not only in electric vehicles, but also in batteries, design and software. The BBC visited factory floors in Beijing and Hefei on the sidelines of Auto China 2026 - the world's largest car show - and found striking levels of automation and software development speed, leaving foreign brands that once dominated the Chinese market struggling to keep up. "We have no chance against this," Honda chief executive Toshihiro Mibe told Japanese media after visiting a highly automated factory in Shanghai. Ford chief executive Jim Farley has also warned that Western carmakers, are "in a fight for our lives" as Chinese rivals expand globally.

Major carmakers including BYD, Chery, Changan, SAIC’s MG brand and FAW’s premium Hongqi all have models in the pipeline designed specifically for export markets — from small hatchbacks for Europe to pickup trucks for Australia and Mexico. At home, Chinese carmakers cram cars with technology and sell them cheaply to compete. In Western markets such as Europe, they can often sell at double the price and still undercut established brands. At the Beijing Auto Show in late April, Hongqi unveiled a small “global SUV” targeted for sale in 80 countries. But the vehicle was primarily designed for urban European buyers, design chief Giles Taylor told Reuters. “That’s the reason why that car exists,” Taylor said.

BYD’s Dolphin G hatchback was designed specifically for Europe and will launch in June. Stella Li, the electric vehicle maker’s number 2 executive, said the model was critical because hatchbacks account for more than 40% of new car sales in parts of southern Europe — a segment that barely exists in China. “If we don’t have the right car in this sector, we lose,” Li said. For many Chinese carmakers, exports are a matter of survival as analysts predict consolidation will thin an industry crowded with more than 100 manufacturers. Vehicle sales in China are expected to remain flat or decline. That excess capacity has already helped make China the world’s largest vehicle exporter, overtaking Japan in 2024.

China’s overcrowded domestic market has been locked in a bruising price war for years, leaving many manufacturers struggling to make money. Overseas markets, by contrast, offer room to grow ― and to charge more ― if Chinese brands can persuade consumers they understand local tastes.

Major carmakers including BYD, Chery, Changan, SAIC’s MG brand and FAW’s premium Hongqi all have models in the pipeline designed specifically for export markets — from small hatchbacks for Europe to pickup trucks for Australia and Mexico.

[Lähde: Digital Journal]
In a sprawling office in Hefei, the eastern Chinese electric vehicle hub, hundreds of employees and several robotic arms sat refining software developed jointly by German behemoth Volkswagen and Chinese EV maker XPeng.

The days when foreign firms saw such partnerships largely as a necessary entrance fee to the world’s largest auto market are long gone.

Legacy overseas brands are now seeking out collaboration, hoping the domestic market’s blistering pace and technological innovation will rub off and boost their competitiveness in China and increasingly, abroad.

VW-XPeng’s China Electronic Architecture (CEA) — software that controls a car’s electronics — was delivered within 18 months, said Frank Han, CEO of Cariad China, VW’s software company.

payload.title: Kiinan autoteollisuus kiristää otettaan sähköautojen maailmanmarkkinoista
payload.summary: Kiinalaiset autonvalmistajat haastavat yhä kovemmin Yhdysvaltojen, Euroopan ja Japanin perinteisiä automerkkejä sähköautoissa, akuissa, ohjelmistoissa ja vientiin suunnitelluissa malleissa.
payload.content:
Kiinalaiset autonvalmistajat ovat nousseet asemaan, jossa perinteiset yhdysvaltalaiset, eurooppalaiset ja japanilaiset merkit joutuvat puolustamaan asemiaan paitsi sähköautoissa myös akuissa, suunnittelussa ja autojen ohjelmistoissa. Tehtailla Pekingissä ja Hefeissä on nähty pitkälle vietyä automaatiota ja nopeaa ohjelmistokehitystä, mikä kertoo kilpailun painopisteen muuttuneen koko autoteollisuuden ekosysteemissä.

## Perinteiset merkit menettävät etumatkaansa

Kiinan automarkkina oli pitkään ulkomaisten valmistajien tärkeä kasvun lähde, mutta asetelma on muuttunut nopeasti. Kiinalaiset kilpailijat määrittävät nyt tahtia erityisesti sähköautoissa ja niihin liittyvässä teknologiassa. Tämä haastaa valmistajia, jotka ovat rakentaneet vahvuutensa polttomoottoriautojen, jälleenmyyntiverkostojen ja vakiintuneiden brändien varaan.

Honda-johtaja Toshihiro Mibe kuvasi japanilaismedialle tilannetta poikkeuksellisen jyrkästi vierailtuaan pitkälle automatisoidussa tehtaassa Shanghaissa. Myös Fordin toimitusjohtaja Jim Farley on varoittanut länsimaisten valmistajien joutuneen erittäin kovaan kamppailuun, kun kiinalaiset merkit laajenevat ulkomaille.

Kiinassa valmistajat kilpailevat täyttämällä autoja teknologialla ja pitämällä hinnat matalina. Euroopan kaltaisilla länsimarkkinoilla ne voivat silti usein hinnoitella autojaan kotimarkkinoita korkeammalle ja jäädä yhä alle vakiintuneiden kilpailijoiden hintatason.

## Vientimallit suunnitellaan suoraan ulkomaille

Useat suuret kiinalaisvalmistajat, kuten BYD, Chery, Changan, SAIC:n MG ja FAW:n Hongqi, valmistelevat malleja nimenomaan vientimarkkinoille. Valikoimaan kuuluu pieniä viistoperiä Eurooppaan sekä avolava-autoja Australiaan ja Meksikoon.

Hongqi esitteli Pekingin autonäyttelyssä huhtikuun lopulla pienen globaalin katumaasturin, jota on tarkoitus myydä 80 maassa. Malli on kuitenkin suunniteltu erityisesti eurooppalaisia kaupunkiasiakkaita varten. BYD puolestaan tuo kesäkuussa markkinoille Dolphin G -viistoperän, joka on kehitetty Eurooppaa varten.

BYD:n Stella Li on korostanut viistoperien merkitystä Etelä-Euroopassa, jossa ne muodostavat joillakin alueilla yli 40 prosenttia uusien autojen myynnistä. Segmentti on Kiinassa pieni, mutta Euroopassa sen sivuuttaminen voisi merkitä tärkeän markkinaosuuden menettämistä.

Viennin taustalla on myös paine Kiinan kotimarkkinoilla. Maassa toimii yli sata autonvalmistajaa, ja analyytikot odottavat alan yhdistyvän, kun myynti Kiinassa pysyy paikallaan tai laskee. Ylikapasiteetti on jo auttanut Kiinaa nousemaan maailman suurimmaksi ajoneuvojen viejäksi Japanin ohi vuonna 2024.
summary_bullets: Kiinalaiset autonvalmistajat haastavat perinteisiä länsimaisia ja japanilaisia merkkejä sähköautoissa, akuissa ja ohjelmistoissa.
Useat kiinalaismerkit suunnittelevat malleja suoraan vientimarkkinoille, kuten Eurooppaan, Australiaan ja Meksikoon.
Kiinan kotimarkkinoiden ylikapasiteetti ja kova kilpailu lisäävät painetta kasvattaa vientiä.

article.source_text:
The BBC visited China’s EV factories and found they are dominating the ecosystems shaping the global auto industry.

Global carmakers are facing a reckoning as US, European and Japanese brands lose ground to Chinese rivals setting the pace not only in electric vehicles, but also in batteries, design and software. The BBC visited factory floors in Beijing and Hefei on the sidelines of Auto China 2026 - the world's largest car show - and found striking levels of automation and software development speed, leaving foreign brands that once dominated the Chinese market struggling to keep up. "We have no chance against this," Honda chief executive Toshihiro Mibe told Japanese media after visiting a highly automated factory in Shanghai. Ford chief executive Jim Farley has also warned that Western carmakers, are "in a fight for our lives" as Chinese rivals expand globally.

Major carmakers including BYD, Chery, Changan, SAIC’s MG brand and FAW’s premium Hongqi all have models in the pipeline designed specifically for export markets — from small hatchbacks for Europe to pickup trucks for Australia and Mexico. At home, Chinese carmakers cram cars with technology and sell them cheaply to compete. In Western markets such as Europe, they can often sell at double the price and still undercut established brands. At the Beijing Auto Show in late April, Hongqi unveiled a small “global SUV” targeted for sale in 80 countries. But the vehicle was primarily designed for urban European buyers, design chief Giles Taylor told Reuters. “That’s the reason why that car exists,” Taylor said.

BYD’s Dolphin G hatchback was designed specifically for Europe and will launch in June. Stella Li, the electric vehicle maker’s number 2 executive, said the model was critical because hatchbacks account for more than 40% of new car sales in parts of southern Europe — a segment that barely exists in China. “If we don’t have the right car in this sector, we lose,” Li said. For many Chinese carmakers, exports are a matter of survival as analysts predict consolidation will thin an industry crowded with more than 100 manufacturers. Vehicle sales in China are expected to remain flat or decline. That excess capacity has already helped make China the world’s largest vehicle exporter, overtaking Japan in 2024.
